utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, did you take part in the on-site investigation of the incident of 25th October 1995, the shooting of a tram? The 25th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume so. But if you tell me exactly the location --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The crossroads of Zmaja od Bosne Street and Hamdija Cemerlic Street, the Brotherhood Road. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this incident, there were nine casualties; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the direction of the tram, its orientation?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Do you have the on-site investigation report? Maybe I can take a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that is an official note, 65 ter 10512, document 10512. 10512, and you can see your name appearing under number 4 there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I believe this is P1756, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 8, please, of the document itself. The English page may be different, but we'll see in a moment. Yes, that is the page that I want.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see here, under number 4, where it says: "The crime technician of the Sarajevo CSB, Bogdan Vidovic"? Correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this report so that you can answer my questions more easily. Yes, now we have the English page as well. Here it says that: "An on-site investigation was carried out at the scene at Vojvode Putnika Street, right after the Pofalici tram stop. More specifically, the stretch of the tracks across from the Bellamy Cafe." That's where the Orthodox Church is; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you were able to locate it, can we now have the map again, 1D2581. And if you could please mark that spot. And could it be, please, noted that the witness answered with a "Yes," and the transcript did not reflect that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters cannot hear the witness when the answers are very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the section of the map depicting the point where the incident occurred? And would you please mark the incident location?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hamdija Cemerlic and Zmaja od Bosne Street, that's this intersection here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please be a little bit more precise? It was across from the Bellamy building and the Orthodox Church. Could you please mark Bristol Hotel, the Orthodox Church, and the Bellamy Cafe, and indicate them with numbers 1, 2 and 3?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 2, 3, and 4 for these three buildings and number 1 as the incident location.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know where the Bristol Hotel was. I think it's about here [marks]. The Orthodox Church is here, number 3 [marks], and Bellamy would be about here, I think [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please put number 1 as the incident location?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you recall now the orientation? Which way was the tram going?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that I remember this at all. I do see that I took part in the on-site investigation. However, I can't recall and I don't know what it says in there. Is there a report that I can see?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please -- could I ask again for a hard copy of this, kindly?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I do have a hard copy. Again, I'm worried about setting some kind of precedent with the Prosecution is expected to show up with hard copies during the Defence cross-examination. Perhaps Mr. Karadzic could ask members of his own team to prepare these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I thought it was the witness that asked for the hard copy. Now I understand you. Yes, that can be done on an exceptional basis.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is my understanding that this is a Prosecution witness. And since the witness asked for a hard copy in order to jog his memory, I assume that the Prosecution had prepared a copy of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, please just use that report and tell us whether you can see in which direction this tram was moving. Is it correct that the tram was moving from Bascarsija towards the tram sheds?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear your answer, Mr. Vidovic. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just asked for your understanding. I just want to leaf through this. Since I don't see a single report that I drafted, I will have to read these other reports that were drafted by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I can help you. It says here that it's in line with Sibenska Street, approximately. Maybe that can help you. So it's in line with Sibenska Street which is between the Orthodox Church and the Bellamy Cafe, so that's possibly the 425th street; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near number 3. I really can't recall what the street name was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I can read what it says in this report for you. On page 1, the one-before-last paragraph, the first page of the report, which is the eighth page of the document, it says that: "Immediately after the tram stop at Pofalici, more specifically, on the stretch across from the Bellamy Cafe and the Orthodox Church, between these two facilities there is Sibenska Street, at the beginning of which lies an apartment building that can be reached by a paved road. Sibenska Street is at a 90-degree angle to Vojvode Putnika Street, and approaches to it are closed with several concrete blocks that are 190 centimetres tall and that have -- that are not one next to the other. In the back of this building -- of this street, there is a three-storey building some 120 metres away from the incident site."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps Your Honours would prefer to see an English translation on your screens. If you wish, I can give the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now we're watching the map which has been marked --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- just to refresh the memory of the witness. Did you find the passage, Mr. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But now can you remember in which direction the tram was moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, based on this, from what I could read here, the tram ended up in the tram sheds. I assumed that it was moving from Bascarsija toward Alipasino Polje, towards the so-called "remiza" [phoen] or tram sheds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark with an arrow the orientation of the tram, because the participants here are not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it was moving from east to west; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this would be the direction in which the tram was moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I will try to assist you. Does it help, what it says here, that between the Bellamy Cafe and the Orthodox Church lies the Sibenska Street? Would that assist you in determining more accurately the incident site?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that case, that would be this street here [indicates] next to number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it marked with number 425?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so. I don't know what the name of that street is, either today or then. I really can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it should be noted in the report. It says there that it's Sibenska Street and that the Sibenska Street -- the approach to Sibenska Street from Vojvode Putnika Street was cut off or closed off with some screens, a concrete screen which was 190 centimetres tall?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that it's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you remember how far these concrete block were, one from the other?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. Maybe they're overlapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, now, no, that's not what it says in the report.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let's see what it says on the following page of the report. Please take a look at the second page of the report. In the vicinity, the casing of a 7.62 bullet was found on the floor, the fragmentation bullet. It was handed to over to a ballistic expert for analysis. Can you tell me, in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, was there ever a 7.62-millimetre fragmentation bullet in use?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember. This is not my report at all. It was a report compiled by a colleague of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you participated in the investigation number 4?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was on the site, but it is also possible that I did not draft the report itself, because there were other scene-of-crime technicians there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says the third bullet penetrated the wall of the tram 30 centimetres above the floor, creating a hole 8 centimetres wide --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please slow down. The interpreters cannot cope. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Karadzic, the interpreters were not able to follow you at all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it says here, on page 9: "The third bullet penetrated --" Can you read it yourself?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please read this passage carefully, all the way where it says "part of the lower support of the seat." Maybe I can be of assistance. Does it not state here, unequivocally, that the third bullet entered 30 centimetres above the floor and that the support of the seat was hit at 25 centimetres' height? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D02582. It's the sketch that should correspond to what is written here. But before that - I apologise - can we have this map signed and dated and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date and your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D793, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Just purely for my reference, Mr. Gaynor, the report referred to and admitted as P1756 was admitted as part of an associated exhibit, as forming the indispensable and inseparable part of the amalgamated statement of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And my note says it's referred to in his statement on pages from 58 to 60; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, it's referred to in footnote 26, I believe, which is on page 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this was raised during the cross-examination of the witness done by Mr. Tapuskovic? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, that appears to be the case, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you tender this document to support unscheduled sniping, you're saying, not in order to prove or support the unscheduled sniping but just tender the document which was raised and discussed during the cross-examination in the previous hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. The approach we took on the documents raised during the cross-examination previously is that we included them, really, out of a sense of fairness, that they are raised and discussed during the witness's cross-examination in his previous evidence. It's similarly with a couple of ABiH documents and the document from President Izetbegovic. We included them, really, out of a sense of fairness. Now, Your Honours have admitted them. If Your Honours, as I said when Mr. Vidovic began his testimony, if Your Honours wish not to admit such documents, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So there was a misunderstanding when I said that the Prosecution has tendered this in order to prove to show the pattern or those things?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't think we take such a strict view. We put in the evidence, and it is from that body of evidence that the Court can draw its conclusions and on which we will base our arguments. Now, whether it was admitted during the examination-in-chief or during the cross-examination of the witness in his prior evidence would not, I submit, limit us from relying on that in support of the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, does this mean that the bullet entered the tram at 30 centimetres from the floor and hit the next seat at 25 centimetres from the floor? Does this sketch correspond to what I said? These measurements are expressed in millimetres, so 300 millimetres and 250?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When we have two points of reference, so you can draw a straight line between them?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that that would constitute a 20-degree angle with relation to the floor?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this sketch admitted into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we're dealing with this sketch, I object to the admission of this. Again, this is a document prepared by a member of the Defence team for Mr. Karadzic for the purpose of these proceedings. If he wants to submit it, he can submit it through another form, rather than through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree -- we agree, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall proceed, but we do agree on the angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In light of the point I raised with Mr. Gaynor, I don't think you need to go through these reports in such detail.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D2580, a Google image of this part of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this part of the city, and can you mark what we discussed before? You can see the church, you can see the streets named in your report?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say again that this is not my report, where these streets are mentioned, but I can do the same what I did with the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you can see the church, the Bellamy Cafe, and Sibenska Street between them?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. So that would be it, number 4 [marks], Bristol Hotel. Number 3, the Orthodox Church [marks]. And the -- I'm sorry. Number 2 [marks], and the incident site, number 1 [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It says that with respect to this street, at about 120 metres, which is actually 200 metres, there is a building. Is this the reference to the building that closes Sibenska Street on the Serbian side, and can you mark that building?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the street between 2 and 3, there is nothing blocking it. It connects to Vilsonovo Setaliste.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But on the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several buildings. I can mark the closest one, this one here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says then that the closest skyscraper is 250 metres from the incident site. Can you mark this high-rise building?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know which one they're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the report, what the report says about the layout of these buildings? On page 1, which is page 8 in the document, it says that at about 120 metres from the incident site, and behind it there is a high-rise building at an indefinite distance. But we can see here that it cannot be less than 250 metres. Do you see these square buildings to the left?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to these buildings [indicates]?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm referring to the ones at the very bottom of this image, because these do not have a direct line of site with respect to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to find which high-rise building they are referring to. Perhaps this one here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's say if this building is 120 metres far away, then this would be 250 metres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's say so, although --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put the date and your initials?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this high-rise building marked on the left -- can this marking be erased, because it's wrong, the one next to the river?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Karadzic could explain, for the record, why he believes that's wrong, and the witness could be given an opportunity to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm guided by the report, which says that along Sibenska Street, which is located between the church and Bellamy, the only buildings can be seen from Sibenska Street are the ones here. Sibenska Street is between features 2 and 3 and overlooks number 1, where the incident occurred, and only these buildings can be seen from that particular street, not any other building which is far away. Can we have this document admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D794, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D02583.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You would remember that we agreed that 30 centimetres and 25 centimetres make a 20-degree angle with respect to the floor of the tram?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D02583. Has this Google image been given a number? 1D02583, here we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, do you agree that from the point of impact to this smaller building, there is the distance of around 200 metres, and that a maximum 250 metres to the high-rise building?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what's written on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that a 20-degree angle would indicate that the origin of fire was at 72 metres from the small building and 90 metres from the high-rise building? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say much off the top of my head. But on the basis of this sketch, that would be approximately right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if the angle of descent was 20, the incident angle would require that height. Can we have this admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Again, we'll not admit this document. We allowed you to put the question and elicit the answer from the witness, but it's not appropriate to admit this through this witness. He cannot confirm this drawing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at 65 ter 10512, page 14. 10512, please. This is a part of the report. This is a part of the report. Let's say from the 24th line to the 18th line, where it says: "The first initial damage is located --" Yes, perhaps we can look at a copy in each of the languages: "The first damage is located --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly ask to know where the text is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters were not able to hear those parts. Where is it? Could you locate the passage for the benefit of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "The first point of impact ..." [Interpretation] "The first point of impact" is on the English page, and then in the Serbian it's somewhere in the middle. It's about line 24 from the bottom. So in the English, it's: "The first point of impact is on the sheet metal."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I now ask you, sir, to continue reading in the Serbian, and all the parties and the interpreters have the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The second point of impact is on the left sheet metal side of the front car. It is elliptical in form, 0.8 by 1.5 centimetres from the ground and 69 centimetres from the end of the front car, from the articulated section; photograph number 4. The muzzle of the weapon at the moment when the round was fired was to the left and behind the tram; that is, the direction of fire in relation to the left side of the tram extends from back to front, left to right, and from above to below." Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the interpreters to draw the attention to the right side of the screen. All of that is interpreted. Mr. Vidovic is reading literally. It started with: "The first point of impact ...," and then: "The second point of impact ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please continue, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will start from the beginning, from: "The second point of impact ..." "The second point of impact is on the left sheet metal side of the front car. It is elliptical in form, 0.8 by 1.5 centimetres from the ground and 69 centimetres from the end of the front car."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It seems to be an impossibility for the interpreters to follow the speed of reading; in particular, in the French booth, it's impossible at all. I don't see the point in reading all those passages. Put your question, Mr. Karadzic. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Vidovic, I would like to ask you just to refresh your memory with this document to tell us which angles were established for this incoming bullet.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this document is something that I'm seeing for the first time, since it was written by others. And I assume that on the basis of two angles that are being mentioned here, 26 degrees and 28 degrees and then 10 degrees, I really couldn't tell you anything about these angles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let's do it like this, then. This is something that is part of your expertise. Just like we saw in Marin Dvor, when a bullet comes in at 90 degrees, it creates a regular hole in the form or in the shape of a circle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that when it comes in at a lower angle, as it says here, then it creates an elliptical opening in the body of the tram? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: An elliptical shape, this is what the team in which you were in established. So it is elliptical in form, and the dimensions are 0.8 by 1.5 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first point of impact at the back of the tram, an elliptical shape, and then it is 1 metre 29 centimetres distance from the ground and 82 centimetres from the point at which the rear car starts. And we have an angle of 45.57 degrees here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that angle being mentioned anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, when you calculate it, that is what it comes to; is that right? I mean, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the second point of impact is on the left sheet metal side of the front car. It is, again, elliptical in shape, 0.8 by 1.5, and it's 75 centimetres from the ground, and the median value would be 57.67 degrees, so 57 degrees. So the median value would be 51.66 degrees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you agree, then, that -- and look at this whole page, please. And would you then agree that these ballistics experts' findings are that while establishing --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please indicate where he's reading from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters are lost again. You're simply too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I'm under the pressure of time. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you locate the passage first, and then put your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already mentioned that 75 centimetres is from the ground. This is one bullet. The other bullet is 121 centimetres from the ground. And the angles, when they are calculated, are 45.57.1 and the other one would be 57 degrees, making the median value 51.66 degrees. Now I want to put a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, while we have an impact angle like this, which is 20 degrees, at least, in relation to the ground, is it possible that the bullet came from anywhere from the Serbian territory which is closest to that place at a distance of 200 metres?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How tall would this building have to be?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the first building, which is a three-storey building and which is between 120 and 200 metres from the place of incidence, is three storeys high. 20 degrees could not be achieved from that distance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us then look at 65 ter 1052. I apologise to the French booth. I believe that I am making it difficult for them. Can we now look at page 17, please, of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you said you would be able to finish your cross-examination in an hour. An hour has passed. I checked this transcript, but my memory is not clear. Mr. Robinson, I just wanted to check whether you asked for striking out those amalgamated statements -- those parts of the amalgamated statement which deals with this part?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I asked for two other unscheduled incidents, but not this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, can I please ask you to glance at the official notes of Sulejman Pilav?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question. How many more minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would like to use this to complete this incident, and then I would like to move to the incident in the steelworks, just to show a number of photographs just so that we can show this wasn't how -- this didn't happen in the way that the Prosecution is suggesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, do you agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Prosecution is not suggesting anything in relation to the incident. This incident was raised during the cross-examination of this witness by the counsel of Mr. Milosevic or Mr. Milosevic. As I said to you, there's no point of going through this incident in such a detail. I was wondering whether it was a part of this objection by your legal adviser, and we are thinking that we should have granted that request, but it was not requested. Move on to your next topic, and conclude by 35. Then we'll take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- do you agree -- actually, did you participate in this investigation of this incident that we are finishing and which you indicated as being number 4?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did, since I am noted in it. I probably did participate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you read that this Sulejman Pilav confirmed that French experts just waved their hands and said the shots came from Bellamy, not from the Serbian territories? You can see the fifth or sixth line of this statement.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me just read it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreter even said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with what -- I mean, I don't agree, but I agree that that is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have a different opinion? Do you have anything established in this case? Can you please tell me what you established in this case?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ballistics experts did their job. I probably did not do anything else, other than take photographs, in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you recall that on the 9th of March, 1996, you went to investigate at the Ilijas Steelworks?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember that now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D02586, please, so that Mr. Vidovic could refresh his memory. 1D02586.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: Are you familiar with these photographs?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't recall this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please refresh your memory from the report? Is there anything else, other than these photographs? Are these the air-bombs that you found at that location?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that these are naval bombs, not air-bombs?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, really, that is something that I really couldn't tell you anything about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you agree to this report, Mr. Vidovic? You were in a team that established that Serbs had eight air-bombs, which we don't see anywhere in this report. utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Don't make a statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then look at 1D2588.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D2585, page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recall seeing this, but I really don't remember exactly where that was. I perhaps think that it was at this location, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would these wheels shown on the lower photograph possibly belong to those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VIDOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, is it logical to you that the Serbian Army would be using these barrels when it had artillery to fire at where it wanted?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to thank Mr. Vidovic, and I am sorry that we could not throw more light on things. But if you see this barrel, Excellency, where is it that we see explosives here? And all of that is being used against us. What does this prove?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it's not now that you should make a speech or submission. I take it you are minded to tender the previous document, 2586, which refers to the witness as part of the investigation team.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the next one, 2585? I remember the witness confirmed seeing these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, that document is a proofing note of Ekrem Suljevic, and the photographs are attached to that. We have no objection to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And about the last document, the sketch of an aerial bomb, 2588?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There's no indication on that sketch or on the record as to the source of that drawing, of where Mr. Karadzic got that drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the witness said it looks like an aerial bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, although he acknowledged he's never served in the air force or anything like that. As Your Honours wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit them all. If there's a --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask -- may I ask for page 9? If you can just glance at page 9, and perhaps that could be tendered so that you could see what these alleged bombs are. Can we look at page 9 of 02585?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit them all. If there is no English page, we'll mark it for identification. I take it you have some questions for your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
